newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Peru ambassador says no hostage talks yet.
newsitem.headline: Japan Peru ambassador says no hostage talks yet.

text.p: The Japanese ambassador to Peru on Wednesday said he saw no sign of negotiations going on to free about 200 diplomats and businessmen held hostage by leftist guerrillas in the residence in Lima, Japan's foreign minister told a news conference here.

"He said there was no feeling around him inside the residence that negotiations are going on," Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda said of his 10-minute phone call with ambassador Morihisa Aoki at 0930 GMT on Wednesday.
The number of people released by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas was not yet known and the Japanese government had not been in contact with the guerrillas, Ikeda added.
The MRTA rebels have threatened to kill the hostages, including high-ranking foreign diplomats, unless the Peruvian government freed jailed comrades.
Aoki's wife Naoko, who was among the women and elderly people released earlier, told the foreign ministry there were around 600 guests at the party when the armed leftist group launched an attack.
All 10 wives of diplomats who attended the party in honour of Japanese Emperor Akihito's 63rd birthday had been freed, the foreign minister quoted Naoko Aoki as saying.

Ikeda quoted the ambassador as saying there was one injured person in the residence, adding that it was not clear if the injured person was one of the invitees to the reception or one of the guerrillas.
